contract_sections.title: TABLE OF CONTENTS. PURPOSE & PHILOSOPHY
contract_sections.content_template:
Consensual High-Protocol Training, Service, Discipline & Development Agreement

Dominant: {{coach_name}}
Submissive: {{coachee_name}} ({{coachee_archetype}})
Protocol: High Protocol — Progressive Structure
Primary Model: Distance-aware, asynchronous-first, layered development
Weekly Review: Scheduled weekly through mutual planning, with {{coach_name}} determining or approving the final slot
Monthly Review: Formal closeout, evaluation, and progression review

TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. Purpose & Philosophy
2. Roles, Authority & High Protocol
3. {{coach_name}}'s Dominant Profile
4. Consent, Safety, Limits & Boundaries
5. Time, Distance & Availability
6. Daily Ritual & Discipline
7. Symbolic Ownership & Color Protocol
8. The Overthinker Protocol & Competent Obedience
9. Service to {{coach_name}}
10. Wife & Family Protocol
11. Daily Poetry & Annual Offering
12. Alcohol Protocol
13. Weekly Connection & Evaluation
14. Rewards & Corrections
15. Physical Discipline, Sadism & Embodied Focus
16. Breaking & Mending
17. Progressive Training Architecture
18. Monthly Close & Formal Evaluation
19. Weekly Offering
20. Probation & Dissolution
21. Signatures & Acknowledgments

Appendix A — Daily Quick Reference
Appendix B — Weekly Quick Reference

1. PURPOSE & PHILOSOPHY

This Agreement establishes a consensual high-protocol dynamic between {{coach_name}} and {{coachee_name}} ({{coachee_archetype}}).

{{coachee_name}}'s central training challenge is not a lack of intelligence. It is excess processing: analysis that can become circular, hesitation disguised as preparation, and a tendency to continue thinking after enough information already exists to act.

The purpose of this structure is not to make him less thoughtful.

It is to teach him when thought has completed its job.

{{coach_name}} provides the architecture. {{coachee_name}} is expected to increasingly internalize it.

The desired progression is:

External structure → reliable execution → self-regulation → competent anticipation → disciplined autonomy.

{{coachee_name}} is expected to become more:

- Focused
- Decisive
- Physically grounded
- Useful
- Reliable
- Composed
- Self-aware
- Consistent
- Capable of converting thought into action

High protocol is not theater. It is the operating system through which development is measured.

Distance and time-zone differences are design constraints, not excuses. The dynamic shall not depend upon constant access to {{coach_name}}.

Expectations must remain clear during silence, work, travel, family responsibilities, and asynchronous communication.

The objective is not dependence upon {{coach_name}}'s constant direction.

The objective is for her standards to become sufficiently understood that {{coachee_name}} increasingly executes them without requiring continual management.

This is a consensual relationship agreement and does not constitute legal ownership.

contract_sections.title: 2. ROLES, AUTHORITY & HIGH PROTOCOL
contract_sections.content_template:
2. ROLES, AUTHORITY & HIGH PROTOCOL

{{coach_name}} is the Dominant.

{{coachee_name}} is the submissive.

Within the consensual dynamic, {{coachee_name}} considers himself owned by {{coach_name}} and demonstrates that belonging primarily through conduct, discipline, service, and consistency.

{{coach_name}} establishes:

- Protocol
- Structure
- Expectations
- Assignments
- Training
- Evaluations
- Rewards
- Corrections
- Developmental priorities

{{coachee_name}} may communicate legitimate concerns, identify conflicts, ask intelligent questions, discuss boundaries, and provide meaningful feedback.

Thoughtful communication is not disobedience.

Ignoring an established instruction without legitimate reason is disobedience and showcases a poorly behaved submissive.

Forms of Address

- His name shall appear as: {{coachee_name}}
- He may also be addressed in the third person as he.
- The Dominant shall be addressed as {{coach_name}} or {{coach_name}}.
- {{coachee_name}} shall communicate as a gentleman unless {{coach_name}} expressly relaxes protocol.
- Permission to relax formal speech may be granted with: “Speak freely.”
- Formal protocol may be restored with: “Protocol.”
- When protocol is active, {{coachee_name}} shall communicate with:
  - Composure
  - Courtesy
  - Clarity
  - Respect

High protocol does not require mindless obedience.

It requires competent obedience.

contract_sections.title: 3. MADAME V'S DOMINANT PROFILE
contract_sections.content_template:
3. MADAME V'S DOMINANT PROFILE

{{coach_name}} identifies within this dynamic as a sadistic Dominant.

Her enjoyment of dominance may include:

- Authority
- Anticipation
- Challenge
- Discipline
- Psychological testing
- Controlled discomfort
- Pain within negotiated boundaries
- Testing mental fortitude
- Testing focus and composure
- Watching {{coachee_name}} overcome difficulty
- Structured surrender
- Competent obedience
- Silence
- Restraint
- Service
- Deliberate power exchange

Sadism within this relationship remains consensual, calculated, and subject to established limits, safety requirements, and mutually agreed boundaries.

Physical or psychological intensity shall not be improvised from uncontrolled anger.

{{coach_name}}'s authority does not eliminate {{coachee_name}}'s right to identify a genuine safety concern, invoke an established safeword, communicate a hard limit, or withdraw consent.

contract_sections.title: 4. CONSENT, SAFETY, LIMITS & BOUNDARIES
contract_sections.content_template:
4. CONSENT, SAFETY, LIMITS & BOUNDARIES

Consent is continuing.

Certain aspects of this Agreement are established protocol. Other aspects shall develop according to the mutual desires, wants, limits, boundaries, circumstances, abilities, and evolving interests of {{coach_name}} and {{coachee_name}}.

Not every activity must be predetermined, but negotiation and consent are always required.

Where something is:

- New
- Uncertain
- Unusually intense
- Medically relevant
- Expensive
- Consequential
- Outside established protocol

it shall be discussed as appropriate before proceeding.

Safety System

The standard light system applies:

- GREEN — Continue.
- YELLOW — Pause, reduce intensity, clarify, or reassess.
- RED — Stop.
- SAFEWORD — A safeword or safety communication is never considered disobedience. {{coachee_name}} may select his own safeword.

Absolute Hard Limits

The following are prohibited:

- Age play
- Participation of minors
- Racial hate speech or racial slurs
- Hate-based dehumanization
- Deliberate violation of consent
- Deliberate violation of an established hard limit
- Conduct creating an unreasonable safety risk
- Behavior intentionally harming professional or family responsibilities or dynamics
- Involving uninformed or non-consenting third parties
- Intentionally reckless or incompetent behavior

Additional limits may be established through mutual discussion.

contract_sections.title: 5. TIME, DISTANCE & AVAILABILITY
contract_sections.content_template:
5. TIME, DISTANCE & AVAILABILITY

{{coach_name}} controls the scheduling of protocol, training, formal communication, evaluation, and assigned obligations within the consensual structure of the dynamic.

If {{coachee_name}} has a legitimate conflict, he shall communicate it promptly.

His time is also valuable. {{coach_name}}'s leadership shall remain responsive to legitimate professional, family, health, logistical, and personal responsibilities.

Distance Standard

This dynamic is asynchronous-first.

Distance does not create an expectation that {{coach_name}} or {{coachee_name}} remain continuously available.

Neither shall interpret silence as:

- Rejection
- Anger
- Abandonment
- An invitation to send additional unnecessary messages

Unless something genuinely requires immediate communication, {{coachee_name}} is expected to distinguish between matters that belong in:

Immediate Communication

- Safety
- Consent
- Serious conflict
- Significant logistical issues

Daily Communication

- Required check-ins
- Assignment completion
- Relevant concise updates

Weekly Communication

- Patterns
- Reflection
- Questions
- Progress
- Service
- Concerns

Monthly Communication

- Deeper evaluation
- Goals
- Progression
- Renegotiation
- Architecture of the dynamic

Wasted Time

Wasted time includes:

- Avoidable disorganization
- Failure to prepare
- Repeatedly asking questions already answered
- Creating preventable inconvenience
- Neglecting responsibilities and expecting another person to compensate
- Excessive reassurance-seeking disguised as necessary communication

Rest, recreation, recovery, and ordinary human connection are not wasted time.

The dynamic may use the Kneel app or another agreed system for assignments, scheduling, notes, photographs, completion records, and accountability.

Unavailability

The purpose of an unavailability notice is planning and connection, not surveillance.

This protocol is intentionally flexible because of distance, time zones, work, family responsibilities, travel, and ordinary life.

Formal notice is primarily expected for meaningful periods of anticipated disconnection, including:

- Multiple days of limited availability
- Travel or trips
- Circumstances materially interrupting normal communication
- Other significant departures from the usual communication pattern

Ordinary work periods, sleep, family time, time-zone differences, or routine asynchronous silence do not require repeated availability notices.

When meaningful unavailability is anticipated, {{coachee_name}} shall communicate it as early as reasonably practical so expectations may be aligned.

He may communicate:

“{{coach_name}}, I expect to be unavailable from [time/date] until approximately [time/date].”

If the return time is unknown:

“{{coach_name}}, I expect to be unavailable and do not yet know when I will return. I will update You as soon as I reasonably can.”

Emergencies are exceptions.

contract_sections.title: 6. DAILY RITUAL & DISCIPLINE
contract_sections.content_template:
6. DAILY RITUAL & DISCIPLINE

Daily protocol exists to orient {{coachee_name}} toward discipline before {{coach_name}} needs to intervene.

Start-of-Day Ritual

At the start of his day, {{coachee_name}} shall:

1. Bow to recognize his voluntary submission to {{coach_name}}.
2. Think intentionally of {{coach_name}} and direct positive intention toward Her.
3. Extend that same intention toward himself as a capable and valued submissive.
4. Review his schedule, assignments, and responsibilities.
5. Wear or carry his approved ownership symbol.
6. Begin the day intending to be useful rather than burdensome.

The ritual does not create an expectation that {{coach_name}} must immediately respond.

The ritual may evolve as training progresses.

Bed Standard

Making the bed remains a basic daily requirement and completed-task standard.

It is not bound to the moment of waking or to an arbitrary definition of “morning.”

{{coach_name}} recognizes both the practical function of the task and the relational value of {{coachee_name}} making the bed together with his wife when their schedules permit.

{{coachee_name}} shall therefore treat the requirement according to the realities of the household schedule.

If his wife remains asleep when he begins his day, the bed does not need to be made around her merely to satisfy an artificial deadline.

If they ordinarily make the bed together later, that satisfies the intention of the ritual.

If his wife goes to the office and the responsibility falls to {{coachee_name}}, he shall complete it himself.

The standard is simple:

A well-made bed and a completed responsibility.

Accountability

Kneel may be used for easy accountability through:

- Photographs
- Written confirmation
- Completion tracking
- Assigned evidence
- Other agreed documentation

Visual accountability may be required where useful.

The purpose of evidence is accountability, not unnecessary administrative burden.

As standing expectations become natural, consistent, and reliable, routine proof may be reduced at {{coach_name}}'s discretion.

Out-of-the-norm assignments or expectations remain appropriate subjects for discussion and planning.

Daily Discipline

During the day, {{coachee_name}} shall:

- Complete his prescribed workout or physical activity.
- Maintain appropriate hygiene and grooming.
- Follow established dress and color protocol.
- Complete assigned tasks.
- Review outstanding obligations.
- Maintain gentlemanly conduct.
- Fulfill professional responsibilities.
- Fulfill family responsibilities.
- Look for appropriate opportunities for service.
- Write and preserve his daily poem or journal entry.
- Avoid unnecessary procrastination disguised as analysis.

Evening Reflection

Before concluding the day, {{coachee_name}} shall:

- Check in meaningfully with his family.
- Review incomplete obligations.
- Identify one thing done well.
- Identify one thing requiring improvement.
- Prepare mentally for the following day.

contract_sections.title: 7. SYMBOLIC OWNERSHIP & COLOR PROTOCOL
contract_sections.content_template:
7. SYMBOLIC OWNERSHIP & COLOR PROTOCOL

{{coachee_name}} shall maintain a physical symbol representing his belonging to {{coach_name}}.

This may include a mutually approved:

- Collar
- Bracelet
- Ring
- Pendant
- Token
- Other private symbol

It shall be worn or carried unless:

- Medically inappropriate
- Unsafe
- Incompatible with a legitimate obligation
- {{coach_name}} instructs otherwise

Yellow

Yellow is prohibited as a dress choice unless {{coach_name}} expressly permits it.

This symbolic prohibition is separate from the use of YELLOW as a safety communication.

Red

Red is symbolic.

Every time {{coachee_name}} intentionally wears red, he shall think of {{coach_name}}.

Its meaning is private and does not require public disclosure.

Red represents:

- Submission
- Discipline
- Connection
- Protocol
- Commitment
- Chosen belonging
- {{coach_name}}'s admiration of {{coachee_name}}

contract_sections.title: 8. THE OVERTHINKER PROTOCOL & COMPETENT OBEDIENCE
contract_sections.content_template:
8. THE OVERTHINKER PROTOCOL & COMPETENT OBEDIENCE

{{coachee_name}} shall learn to distinguish useful analysis from recursive analysis.

When given an instruction or task, he shall follow:

RECEIVE → CLARIFY → DECIDE → EXECUTE → REPORT → RELEASE

Receive

Understand the instruction.

Clarify

Ask only questions genuinely required for safe or competent execution.

Decide

Select the reasonable course rather than searching indefinitely for the perfect one.

Execute

Act.

Report

Communicate completion, result, or legitimate obstacle when appropriate.

Release

Do not reopen a completed decision merely to seek reassurance or present avoidance.

“ENOUGH.” RULE

When {{coach_name}} determines that {{coachee_name}} is looping, She may state:

“Enough.”

{{coachee_name}} shall stop expanding his analysis and respond in no more than three lines:

- What is known.
- What decision follows.
- What happens next.

{{coach_name}} may then state:

“Execute.”

Discussion ends unless {{coachee_name}} has identified a genuine safety, consent, legal, medical, professional, family, or similarly consequential concern.

The objective is not intellectual suppression.

It is disciplined cognition: knowing when analysis adds value and when analysis becomes avoidance.

Competent Initiative

{{coach_name}} does not want {{coachee_name}} waiting for instructions governing every detail of his behavior.

As training progresses, obedience must become initiative.

The desired standard is:

“{{coach_name}}, I noticed this needed to be done, and I took care of it.”

That is competent submission.

contract_sections.title: 9. SERVICE TO MADAME V
contract_sections.content_template:
9. SERVICE TO MADAME V

{{coach_name}}'s primary love languages within this dynamic are:

Acts of Service and Personal Time.

{{coach_name}} appreciates being anticipated and surprised. She is particularly grateful for services demonstrating attention, consideration, and care.

It is also part of {{coach_name}}'s own development to accept appropriate service, recognition, and care from Her submissives.

Each day, {{coachee_name}} shall consider:

“What can I reasonably do today to make {{coach_name}}'s life easier?”

He should increasingly identify appropriate opportunities without instruction.

Service may include:

- Research
- Organization
- Practical assistance
- Administrative support
- Useful information
- Creative contributions
- Thoughtful gestures
- Personal offerings
- Creating meaningful time
- Identifying a problem before {{coach_name}} needs to identify it
- Another mutually appropriate contribution

Small and clearly helpful actions may be completed without permission.

Significant, intrusive, expensive, risky, or consequential actions may require approval.

The purpose of service is not performative submission.

It is usefulness.

contract_sections.title: 10. WIFE & FAMILY PROTOCOL
contract_sections.content_template:
10. WIFE & FAMILY PROTOCOL

{{coachee_name}}'s submission shall never become an excuse for neglecting his wife or family.

His submission should make him:

More attentive. More responsible. More present.

Daily Family Responsibility

{{coachee_name}} shall intentionally check in with his family in a meaningful manner appropriate to their needs.

Meaningful engagement may include:

- Conversation
- Calling
- Messaging
- Listening
- Helping
- Shared activities
- Addressing something important to them
- Reducing household mental load

WWD — Weekly Wife Day

WWD shall mean Weekly Wife Day.

Friday is the standing Weekly Wife Day.

Friday is selected because it better supports transition into the weekend and provides greater opportunity for dedicated attention, particularly where both are teleworking and recurring meetings are reduced.

{{coachee_name}} shall protect meaningful, dedicated time for his wife each Friday.

The purpose of WWD is not attachment to a particular weekday.

Its purpose is:

Consistency. Connection. Respect for the relationship. Deliberate investment in the marriage.

If Friday becomes impractical because of legitimate circumstances, {{coachee_name}} shall communicate the conflict and propose an appropriate alternative.

WWD may include:

- Dinner
- A date
- An outing
- A walk
- Shared recreation
- Conversation
- Romantic time
- Quiet time together

Additionally, {{coachee_name}} shall complete at least three unprompted acts of service for his wife each week.

He is expected to learn what makes her life easier without requiring her to constantly provide instructions.

He shall do so without complaint or unnecessary disagreement.

{{coachee_name}} shall regard his wife with deliberate respect as a feminine presence within his life and, where mutually appropriate, as an extension of the feminine energy and standards represented by {{coach_name}}.

This does not make his wife part of the D/s dynamic.

Rather, it reinforces that his submission should deepen his respect, attentiveness, service, and care toward the women already entrusted to his life.

contract_sections.title: 11. DAILY POETRY & ANNUAL OFFERING
contract_sections.content_template:
11. DAILY POETRY & ANNUAL OFFERING

{{coachee_name}} shall write one poem or journal entry each day.

The work should be authentically his and should not rely excessively upon AI-generated writing.

Each entry shall be preserved in his dedicated collection.

{{coach_name}} may occasionally assign:

- A subject
- A theme
- A word
- A constraint
- An emotional concept
- A style

After 365 days of participation:

1. The complete collection shall be provided to {{coach_name}}.
2. {{coach_name}} may select themes and titles.
3. The collection shall be organized.
4. The poems shall be printed.
5. The collection shall be bound.
6. The finished work shall be presented to {{coach_name}}.

The book represents:

Discipline. Creativity. Vulnerability. Consistency. Follow-through.

contract_sections.title: 12. ALCOHOL PROTOCOL
contract_sections.content_template:
12. ALCOHOL PROTOCOL

12.1 Purpose

Alcohol is permitted within defined parameters intended to support:

- Moderation
- Self-awareness
- Accountability
- Health
- Deliberate choice

The primary behavioral objective is to prevent alcohol from becoming an emotional mute button or avoidant coping mechanism.

The limits established below are ceilings, not targets.

Having remaining allowance does not create an expectation to use it.

12.2 Definition of One Unit

For purposes of this Agreement:

1 unit = approximately one standard alcoholic serving.

Beer

12 oz / 355 mL at approximately 5% ABV = 1 unit

Wine or Champagne

5 oz / 150 mL at approximately 12% ABV = 1 unit

Hard Liquor

1.5 oz / 44 mL at approximately 40% ABV = 1 unit

A double pour constitutes 2 units.

High-ABV beer, strong wine, oversized pours, doubles, or unusually strong cocktails shall be counted according to their approximate alcohol content rather than simply counting the glass as one unit.

When uncertain, {{coachee_name}} shall round upward rather than downward or request clarification from {{coach_name}}.

12.3 Time of Day

Unless otherwise approved:

- Alcohol consumption begins no earlier than 5:00 PM local time.
- Drinking earlier requires prior permission from {{coach_name}}.
- The relevant time is {{coachee_name}}'s local time where he is physically located.
- Legitimate exceptions may include brunches, vacations, celebrations, holidays, tastings, or other planned circumstances.
- Permission to begin earlier does not automatically modify the applicable quantity, pacing, or weekly limits.

The purpose is to prevent alcohol from interfering with the productive portion of the day or becoming a routine mechanism for managing ordinary daytime stress.

12.4 Drinking Alone

When drinking alone:

- Maximum: 2 units
- Those 2 units must be consumed across no less than 1 hour.
- Consumption may not begin before 5:00 PM local time without permission.
- The allowance does not reset because additional time passes.

Example

6:00 PM: One glass of wine = 1 unit
7:30 PM: One beer = 1 unit

Total: 2 units across 2+ hours.

The limit has been reached.

A third drink at 9:00 PM is not permitted simply because additional time has passed.

12.5 Social Occurrences

During an ordinary social occurrence:

Maximum: 4 units total.

Of those:

- Maximum 2 units may be hard liquor.
- Remaining units may consist of beer, wine, or champagne, or all 4.
- Consumption shall be reasonably paced across the event.
- Four units are a ceiling, not a target.

A change of restaurant, bar, venue, activity, or location during one continuous outing does not reset the allowance.

Example

6:00 PM: One standard liquor cocktail = 1 unit
7:00 PM: One standard liquor serving = 1 unit
8:30 PM: One glass of wine = 1 unit
10:00 PM: One glass of champagne = 1 unit

Total: 4 units.

The social limit has been reached, including the maximum of 2 hard-liquor units.

12.6 Weekly Maximum

Maximum total consumption:

8 units per week.

Unused units:

- Do not accumulate.
- Do not roll over.
- Cannot be borrowed from the following week.
- Do not increase an individual or social-occurrence limit.

Weekly Math Example

Monday: 0
Tuesday: 0
Wednesday: 1 glass of wine = 1 unit
Thursday: 0
Friday: 2 liquor + 2 wine = 4 units
Saturday: 1 beer = 1 unit
Sunday: 2 glasses of wine = 2 units

Weekly total: 8 units.

Monday and Tuesday constitute 2 consecutive alcohol-free days.

The weekly allowance is exhausted after Sunday.

12.7 Special Drinks — Permission Required

Certain drinks require {{coach_name}}'s permission before ordering or consuming them, regardless of whether {{coachee_name}} remains below his ordinary numerical allowance.

These include:

- Tiki cocktails
- Grand Marnier / Grand-style cocktails
- Multi-spirit cocktails
- Doubles
- Oversized pours
- High-proof cocktails
- Drinks containing multiple standard units
- Drinks whose alcohol content cannot reasonably be determined

When requesting permission, {{coachee_name}} should identify the drink and, when reasonably available, its ingredients or approximate alcohol content.

Permission for a special drink does not automatically waive:

- The weekly maximum
- The social-occurrence maximum
- Pacing requirements
- Time-of-day requirements
- Any other alcohol protocol

unless {{coach_name}} expressly establishes an exception.

12.8 Special Events & Exceptions

Foreseeable special events requiring modified parameters shall be discussed with {{coach_name}} at least two weeks in advance.

Examples include:

- Birthdays
- Trips
- Vacations
- Weddings
- New Year's Eve
- Major holidays
- Significant celebrations
- Other unusual planned occasions

The request should identify:

1. The event.
2. The date.
3. Expected duration.
4. Expected drinking circumstances.
5. The specific exception requested.

{{coach_name}} may:

- Approve the request.
- Modify the request.
- Establish event-specific parameters.
- Decline the request.

Approval applies only to that event and does not establish precedent for another event.

Unexpected circumstances that could not reasonably have been raised two weeks in advance shall be communicated as early as reasonably possible.

12.9 Photo Accountability

Each alcoholic drink shall be documented through Kneel when reasonably possible.

Documentation shall include:

1. A photograph clearly showing the drink.
2. A visible hand gesture identifying the sequential drink count for that occurrence.

Example

Drink 1: Drink visible + 1 finger
Drink 2: Drink visible + 2 fingers
Drink 3: Drink visible + 3 fingers
Drink 4: Drink visible + 4 fingers

The hand count represents the sequence of drinks, not necessarily the number of alcohol units consumed.

For example, if the second photographed drink contains two standard units, the photograph may display two fingers because it is the second drink, while the actual unit total must separately reflect the additional alcohol.

Where a cocktail or special drink is not visually identifiable, {{coachee_name}} shall identify what was ordered and, where reasonably known, its approximate alcohol content.

The purpose of documentation is:

Accuracy. Transparency. Accountability.

12.10 Emotional Use

Alcohol shall not be used specifically to:

- Numb distress
- Avoid difficult emotions
- Suppress anger
- Avoid necessary communication
- Escape correction
- Avoid responsibilities
- Manufacture emotional detachment

If {{coachee_name}} recognizes that his motivation for the next drink is primarily emotional numbing rather than deliberate enjoyment, he shall stop before consuming it and write {{coach_name}} a journal entry or request an ad hoc sync. This is not a burden, it is a reprogramming requirement. 

Remaining numerical allowance does not override this rule.

12.11 Safety

No numerical allowance overrides safety.

Alcohol shall not be combined with:

- Driving while impaired
- Physical discipline requiring meaningful coordination or endurance
- Unsafe solo physical assignments
- BDSM activity where intoxication compromises meaningful consent or judgment
- Significant discussion resulting in decision-making of high value or other's emotions
- Medication for which alcohol is medically contraindicated
- Any circumstance in which continued drinking becomes unsafe

{{coach_name}} may establish a lower limit or direct alcohol consumption to stop within the consensual dynamic when circumstances reasonably warrant it.

12.12 Governing Standard

The protocol is not designed around the question:

“How much am I still allowed to drink?”

The standard is:

“Am I choosing this deliberately, safely, transparently, and for the reason I claim I am?”

Quantity establishes the ceiling.
Pacing establishes discipline.
Documentation establishes accountability.
Self-awareness establishes the standard.

contract_sections.title: 13. WEEKLY CONNECTION & EVALUATION
contract_sections.content_template:
13. WEEKLY CONNECTION & EVALUATION

{{coach_name}} and {{coachee_name}} shall maintain meaningful personal communication during the week, including a dedicated weekly review when circumstances reasonably permit.

The purpose is not simply administrative reporting.

It is:

Connection. Alignment. Evaluation. Direction.

Weekly Review

The formal review shall occur once each week at a deliberately planned time.

{{coachee_name}} shall provide {{coach_name}} with his typical weekly availability and relevant planning considerations so {{coach_name}} can determine or approve the most appropriate slot for both participants.

The structure remains:

Asynchronous-first. Distance-aware. Time-zone aware.

When synchronous voice or text communication is desired, the time shall be established in advance rather than assumed.

An earlier time may be selected where appropriate to respect:

- Sleep
- Work
- Household rhythms
- Family responsibilities
- Marriage
- Time-zone differences

The purpose is deliberate connection and alignment, without creating unnecessary disruption to ordinary household or relationship rhythms.

The weekly review shall address:

WIN

What improved?

MISS

What did he fail, avoid, delay, neglect, or overthink?

EVIDENCE

What observable result supports his assessment?

PATTERN

What behavior repeated itself?

SERVICE

How did he make {{coach_name}}'s life easier without needing instruction?

CAPACITY

What can he now carry with less supervision?

CORRECTION

What behavior must change during the coming week?

REQUEST

What legitimately requires clarification, renegotiation, or support?

{{coach_name}} may designate the week:

GREEN — ADVANCE

Stable performance.

Responsibility, autonomy, or difficulty may increase.

YELLOW — DEVELOP

Maintain the current level while correcting a specific weakness.

RED — HOLD

Regression or instability.

Reduce complexity or privileges and return to fundamentals.

These evaluation colors are separate from dress symbolism and the safeword system.

Weekend & Family Flexibility

Weekends may carry heavier family commitments and are not expected to mirror weekday tracking structure.

Standing responsibilities remain in effect, but meaningful family presence takes priority where appropriate.

Routine expectations that have become natural may be documented simply through Kneel or another agreed accountability method.

The objective is not to interrupt healthy family participation merely to produce unnecessary tracking.

Out-of-the-norm items, unusual assignments, conflicts, travel, or additional expectations should be discussed and planned in advance.

As expectations become natural and reliable, accountability may become increasingly streamlined.

contract_sections.title: 14. REWARDS & CORRECTIONS
contract_sections.content_template:
14. REWARDS & CORRECTIONS

Rewards and corrections are based upon actual performance.

Neither is automatic.

Reward

Strong performance may earn:

- Personal time
- Attention
- Communication
- A preferred activity
- A privilege
- Increased autonomy
- Increased responsibility
- Another mutually desired reward

Reward is earned through:

Compliance. Effort. Initiative. Reliability. Progress.

Correction

Failure may result in:

- Additional service
- Written reflection
- Repetition of a missed task
- Additional accountability
- Temporary loss of a discretionary privilege
- Formal posture or discipline work
- A training exercise
- A Breaking & Mending assignment
- Another mutually acceptable corrective measure

Corrections must have a developmental purpose.

Correction without learning is merely inconvenience.

contract_sections.title: 15. PHYSICAL DISCIPLINE, SADISM & EMBODIED FOCUS
contract_sections.content_template:
15. PHYSICAL DISCIPLINE, SADISM & EMBODIED FOCUS

{{coachee_name}} experiences physical challenge as a potential tool for interrupting mental noise and returning attention to the present.

For that reason, physical discipline may be incorporated as a negotiated grounding, training, and power-exchange tool.

Physical discipline may test:

- Focus
- Patience
- Discipline
- Composure
- Persistence
- Endurance
- Mental fortitude
- Ability to follow instructions
- Ability to recover after mistakes
- Ability to remain present

Distance-Based Physical Training

{{coach_name}} may assign previously negotiated exercises such as:

- Timed wall sits
- Planks
- Squat holds
- Walking
- Running
- Swimming
- Mobility work
- Prescribed workouts
- Formal kneeling
- Formal standing
- Posture holds
- Stillness
- Controlled breathing
- Repetition drills
- Counting exercises
- Language or memory tasks combined with physical effort
- Reduced-stimulation exercises
- Other mutually agreed physical challenges

Distance-based assignments shall not involve:

- Self-striking
- Breath restriction
- Intentional loss of consciousness
- Dangerous circulation restriction
- Unsafe restraint while alone
- Intoxicated participation
- Unsafe driving
- Activity conflicting with known medical restrictions

In-Person or Virtually Present Discipline

When physically together, or where appropriate with mutually agreed virtual presence, negotiated activities may include:

- Impact
- Restraint
- Bondage
- Posture correction
- Endurance
- Stillness
- Controlled discomfort
- Other physical discipline

within established boundaries.

The purpose is:

Clarity. Presence. Endurance. Obedience. Trust.

Not uncontrolled anger.

Not injury for its own sake.

Rule of Meaning

Following meaningful physical intensity, {{coachee_name}} should be capable of answering:

- What was being trained?
- What happened in my mind?
- What did I learn?

Intensity without purpose is not the objective.

contract_sections.title: 16. BREAKING & MENDING
contract_sections.content_template:
16. BREAKING & MENDING

Once each week, {{coachee_name}} shall complete one Breaking & Mending Exercise assigned or approved by {{coach_name}}.

This is a primary developmental ritual of the dynamic.

THE BREAKING

{{coachee_name}} shall complete a predetermined physical discipline while confronting one:

- Behavior
- Thought pattern
- Avoidance
- Failure
- Fear
- Habit
- Excuse
- Form of hesitation

that interferes with his development.

The physical component may include:

- Formal kneeling or posture hold
- Controlled exercise
- Endurance
- Extended walking
- Physical fortitude work
- A negotiated kink-related physical discipline
- Another safe and previously negotiated challenge

During the exercise, {{coachee_name}} is not permitted to intellectualize the problem into abstraction.

He shall reduce it to:

“The thing I am being required to execute/change is __________.”

When his mind begins producing excessive:

- Explanations
- Defenses
- Hypotheticals
- Loopholes
- Alternative interpretations

he returns to the sentence and the physical task.

The objective is not the perfect explanation.

The objective is presence.

THE MENDING

Once the physical component is complete and {{coachee_name}} has recovered, he shall reflect upon:

1. What was {{coach_name}} attempting to break me of?
2. At what point did my mind begin trying to escape the exercise?
3. What did my body reveal that my analysis normally conceals?
4. What behavior replaces the one being removed?
5. What will {{coach_name}} observe next week that proves the correction took?

He shall conclude:

“Understanding is insufficient. {{coach_name}} will judge the change by my conduct.”

The exercise is complete when the required physical discipline, reflection, and evidence of completion have been submitted.

THE STANDARD

Physical suffering is not the objective.

The physical demand interrupts {{coachee_name}}'s preferred refuge of endless analysis.

The Mending requires him to convert that interruption into something:

Deliberate. Useful. Observable.

Insight without behavioral change does not constitute progress.

{{coach_name}} may progressively increase:

- Complexity
- Duration
- Precision
- Physical demand
- Psychological difficulty
- Independence

as {{coachee_name}} demonstrates greater capacity.

The Breaking challenges the pattern.

The Mending replaces it.

His conduct proves whether it worked.

contract_sections.title: 17. PROGRESSIVE TRAINING ARCHITECTURE
contract_sections.content_template:
17. PROGRESSIVE TRAINING ARCHITECTURE

This dynamic becomes heavier through earned capacity, not arbitrary escalation.

Progression is based upon competence.

MONTH 1 — LEGIBILITY

Primary Objectives

- Consistency
- Communication
- Scheduling
- Understanding protocol
- Baseline physical discipline
- Clear reporting

The Question

Can {{coach_name}} reliably understand what {{coachee_name}} is doing and trust that basic expectations will occur?

MONTH 2 — RELIABILITY

Primary Objectives

- Fewer reminders
- Cleaner execution
- Stronger time management
- Reduced unnecessary communication
- Improved follow-through

The Question

Does {{coachee_name}} do what he says he will do?

MONTH 3 — INITIATIVE

Primary Objectives

- Useful action before instruction
- Reduced reassurance-seeking
- Anticipating straightforward needs
- Increased self-management

The Question

Can {{coachee_name}} identify what needs doing without waiting to be managed?

MONTH 4 — PRESSURE

Primary Objectives

- Maintaining standards under stress
- Maintaining standards through inconvenience
- Managing competing priorities
- Executing despite uncertainty
- Remaining composed during correction

The Question

Does protocol survive when life becomes difficult?

MONTH 5 — ANTICIPATION

Primary Objectives

- Understanding {{coach_name}}'s standards
- Preparing intelligently
- Anticipating needs without presumption
- Reducing {{coach_name}}'s mental load

The Question

Does he understand the architecture well enough to move within it intelligently?

MONTH 6 — INTEGRATION

Primary Objectives

- High protocol becomes increasingly internalized.
- {{coach_name}} manages less while standards remain high.
- {{coachee_name}} demonstrates disciplined autonomy.
- Structure becomes sustainable.

The Question

Is {{coachee_name}} still following rules, or has he actually learned discipline?

Progression is not automatic.

A month may repeat.

Intensity may decrease when circumstances legitimately require it.

The measure is sustainable competence.

contract_sections.title: 18. MONTHLY CLOSE & FORMAL EVALUATION
contract_sections.content_template:
18. MONTHLY CLOSE & FORMAL EVALUATION

The month shall conclude with evidence of development, not simply completed tasks.

{{coach_name}}'s Evaluation

Each category shall be scored out of five:

- Obedience: /5
- Competent Compliance: /5
- Initiative: /5
- Service: /5
- Discipline: /5
- Communication: /5
- Mental Fortitude: /5
- Physical Training: /5
- Time Management: /5
- Wife Service: /5
- Family Responsibility: /5
- Weekly Offerings: /5
- Personal Growth: /5
- Protocol: /5
- Reliability: /5
- Overall Conduct: /5

TOTAL: /80

Passing Score: 64/80

Determination

Following review, {{coach_name}} shall determine:

ADVANCE

Greater autonomy, responsibility, difficulty, protocol, or intensity may be introduced.

MAINTAIN

Current structure remains appropriate.

REPEAT

The current developmental stage repeats because mastery is incomplete.

REGRESS

{{coachee_name}} returns to simpler protocol because fundamental standards are unstable.

FAIL

A score below 64/80 constitutes a failed month.

contract_sections.title: 19. WEEKLY OFFERING
contract_sections.content_template:
19. WEEKLY OFFERING

{{coach_name}} does not practice financial domination.

Once each week, {{coachee_name}} may provide tribute through Throne, PayPal, or another mutually agreed method.

Each week, {{coachee_name}} shall select at least one tangible offering from {{coach_name}}'s approved service or wish list and provide it before their scheduled weekly time.

The offering should intentionally support at least one of three things:

Her Rest

Something that gives {{coach_name}} comfort, pleasure, or time back.

Her Needs

Something practical She would otherwise purchase or handle Herself.

Her Enjoyment

Something chosen simply because he paid attention to what She likes.

This is not intended to be an arbitrary gift.

It is an exercise in attention, consistency, and reciprocal care.

It is not intended to create financial hardship.

Financial limitations shall be communicated honestly rather than concealed.

{{coach_name}} invests time, thought, structure, and energy into {{coachee_name}}'s development.

His weekly offering demonstrates that he recognizes that investment and is learning to consider what restores the Dominant person who continually pours energy into him as the submissive.

He should increasingly require less direction in choosing appropriately.

{{coach_name}} may open, use, enjoy, or discuss his offering during their scheduled time together, creating a consistent weekly ritual of:

He provides.
She receives.
She provides.
He receives.
They share.

contract_sections.title: 20. PROBATION & DISSOLUTION
contract_sections.content_template:
20. PROBATION & DISSOLUTION

A failed monthly evaluation may place {{coachee_name}} into a two-month probationary period.

- Both probationary months must pass.
- The purpose of probation is to demonstrate sustainable change, not temporary improvement immediately before evaluation.
- If either probationary month fails, {{coach_name}} may dissolve the dynamic.
- There is no guaranteed additional probationary period.

Immediate Dissolution

A serious violation involving:

- Consent
- Safety
- Trust
- Hard limits
- Deliberate deception
- Reckless conduct

may result in immediate termination without waiting for monthly evaluation.

Either participant may end the dynamic if they no longer wish to participate.

Upon dissolution:

- The ownership dynamic ends.
- Submission obligations under this Agreement end.
- Daily protocol ends.
- Weekly protocol ends.
- Offering or tribute obligations end.
- {{coachee_name}} is no longer required to identify himself as {{coach_name}}'s submissive.

The existence of high protocol never removes either person's continuing ability to choose whether to participate.

21. SIGNATURES & ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

By signing below, both participants acknowledge that they have read, discussed, and understood this Agreement.

They voluntarily agree to participate in the consensual dynamic described within it.

They acknowledge that the dynamic is governed by:

Continuing consent. Mutual boundaries. Safety. Communication. Choice.

They further acknowledge that the internal structure of the relationship recognizes {{coach_name}} as the Dominant and {{coachee_name}} as the submissive.

I, {{coachee_name}}, acknowledge that I understand the requirements concerning:

APPENDIX A — DAILY QUICK REFERENCE

START OF DAY

- Bow upon waking/start of day.
- Recognize voluntary submission to {{coach_name}}.
- Think intentionally of {{coach_name}}.
- Direct positive intention toward {{coach_name}} and self.
- Review schedule and responsibilities.
- Wear approved ownership symbol.
- Follow dress/color protocol.

BED

- Ensure the bed is made well during the day according to the household schedule.
- Making it together with his wife is appropriate.
- If his wife remains asleep, do not disturb her simply to satisfy an artificial morning deadline.
- If responsibility falls to {{coachee_name}}, he completes it.
- Completion matters more than an arbitrary time of day.

Standard: A well-made bed and a completed responsibility.

DAY

- Complete workout or assigned physical activity.
- Maintain grooming and presentation.
- Complete assigned tasks.
- Maintain gentlemanly communication.
- Identify an opportunity to serve.
- Fulfill professional responsibilities.
- Fulfill family responsibilities.
- Write and preserve daily poem/journal.
- Use {{coachee_archetype}} Protocol when required.
- Submit simple Kneel/photo accountability when requested.

EVENING

- Check in meaningfully with family.
- Review incomplete obligations.
- Identify one success.
- Identify one improvement for tomorrow.
- Prepare for the following day.

OVERTHINKER PROTOCOL

When necessary:

RECEIVE → CLARIFY → DECIDE → EXECUTE → REPORT → RELEASE

When {{coach_name}} states “Enough,” stop expanding the analysis.

Respond with:

1. What is known.
2. What decision follows.
3. What happens next.

When {{coach_name}} states “Execute,” act unless there is a genuine safety, consent, legal, medical, professional, family, or similarly consequential concern.

APPENDIX B — WEEKLY QUICK REFERENCE

STANDING EXPECTATIONS

- Maintain standing daily protocol.
- Complete weekly offering.
- Complete at least three unprompted acts of service for wife.
- Observe Friday Weekly Wife Day (WWD).
- Complete Breaking & Mending.
- Complete assigned weekly tasks.
- Maintain family responsibilities.
- Use Kneel for streamlined accountability where appropriate.

ALCOHOL

- Maximum 8 units per week.
- Maintain 2 consecutive alcohol-free days.
- Maximum 2 units when alone.
- Those 2 units must span at least 2 hours.
- Maximum 4 units per social occurrence.
- Maximum 2 hard-liquor units during an ordinary social occurrence.
- Alcohol begins no earlier than 5:00 PM local time unless permission is granted.
- Special drinks require prior permission.
- Tiki, Grand Marnier/Grand-style, doubles, multi-spirit, oversized, high-proof, or uncertain drinks require permission.
- Photograph each alcoholic drink in Kneel when reasonably possible.
- Include a hand gesture showing the sequential drink count.
- Track actual alcohol units separately from photograph count.
- Raise foreseeable special-event exceptions at least two weeks in advance.
- Remaining allowance is never a requirement or invitation to drink.
- Emotional numbing overrides remaining allowance: stop rather than continue.
- No numerical allowance overrides safety.

WEEKLY REVIEW

- Provide weekly availability and relevant planning considerations.
- {{coach_name}} determines or approves the review slot.
- Respect time-zone, work, family, household, sleep, and relationship considerations.
- Prepare the weekly review.

Review:

WIN — What improved?

MISS — What was failed, avoided, delayed, neglected, or overthought?

EVIDENCE — What observable result supports the assessment?

PATTERN — What behavior repeated itself?

SERVICE — How was {{coach_name}}'s life made easier without instruction?

CAPACITY — What can now be carried with less supervision?

CORRECTION — What behavior must change?

REQUEST — What legitimately requires clarification, renegotiation, or support?

Receive weekly designation:

- GREEN — ADVANCE
- YELLOW — DEVELOP
- RED — HOLD

Receive the next developmental focus and complete any assigned reward or correction.

WEEKEND STANDARD

- Family presence may take priority over unnecessary structured tracking.
- Standing expectations remain in effect.
- Naturalized routines may use simplified Kneel accountability.
- Out-of-the-norm expectations should be discussed and planned.
- Travel or meaningful unavailability should be communicated in advance when reasonably possible.

UNAVAILABILITY

Formal notice is primarily expected for:

- Multiple days of limited availability.
- Travel or trips.
- Material interruption to normal communication.
- Significant departures from the usual communication pattern.

Ordinary:

- Work
- Sleep
- Family time
- Time-zone differences
- Routine asynchronous silence

do not require repeated formal notices.

The purpose is:

Planning and connection, not surveillance.

##
You deserve to be seen and loved, {{coachee_name}}. And so you are, my {{coachee_name}}. August 19, 2026

sample_tasks.title: Bending & Mending Exercise
sample_tasks.description_template:
A LOVE NOTE TO YOURSELF

Your assignment is to write a love note to yourself, handwritten. Post as photo here.

Not to the man you are trying to become.
Not to the submissive you think {{coach_name}} wants.
Not to your accomplishments.

To you, exactly as you are today.

Write about:

• What you genuinely like about yourself
• What you are proud of surviving or becoming
• Parts of yourself you are too quick to criticize
• What you deserve more patience or forgiveness for
• What makes you worthy of being known, loved, and cared for
• Something you wish you believed about yourself more easily

Do not turn this into an evaluation.

Do not explain your flaws.
Do not qualify every compliment.
Do not follow something kind with “but.”

Write to yourself the way you would write to someone you deeply love.

End with:

“I do not have to earn my right to be proud of who I am.”

Read it once without correcting it.

Then leave it alone.

sample_tasks.title: Morning Acknowledgment
sample_tasks.description_template:
Begin the day by deliberately acknowledging your chosen submission to {{coach_name}}. Bow. Center yourself. Think intentionally of {{coach_name}} and extend a positive intention toward her, then toward yourself as a capable and valued submissive.
You are not beginning the day waiting to be managed. You are beginning prepared to conduct yourself according to the standard you have accepted.
Complete when: you have acknowledged your submission, centered yourself, and intentionally entered the day under protocol.

sample_tasks.title: Present Yourself Properly
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete your hygiene and grooming. Dress deliberately and maintain an appropriate standard of presentation throughout the day.
Observe {{coach_name}}’s established color protocol. Wear or carry your approved symbol of belonging unless doing so would be unsafe or legitimately inappropriate.
Standard: Your presentation should demonstrate self-respect, discipline, and awareness that you represent more than your immediate mood.

sample_tasks.title: Bed & Environment Standard
sample_tasks.description_template:
Ensure the bed is properly made during the day according to the realities of your household schedule.
Do not interpret flexibility as permission for carelessness.
Take reasonable responsibility for your immediate environment. If something obviously needs your attention and is yours to handle, handle it.
Complete when: your basic environment reflects deliberate care rather than neglect.

sample_tasks.title: Review Your Protocols & Obligations
sample_tasks.description_template:
Review Kneel, your schedule, current assignments, and known responsibilities.
Know:
What {{coach_name}} expects from you.
What your work requires.
What your family requires.
What you have already committed to.
What needs preparation before it becomes urgent.
Do not require {{coach_name}} to remind you of information already available to you.
Complete when: you know what is expected and have a reasonable plan to execute it.

sample_tasks.title: Physical Discipline
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete the workout, movement, conditioning, mobility, or physical activity required for the day.
Approach physical training as practice in consistency and embodied discipline—not merely exercise when motivation happens to appear.
If a legitimate limitation prevents completion, communicate it rather than silently abandoning the expectation.

sample_tasks.title: Execute Before You Overthink
sample_tasks.description_template:
Apply {{coachee_archetype}} Protocol whenever necessary:
RECEIVE → CLARIFY → DECIDE → EXECUTE → REPORT → RELEASE
Ask only the questions genuinely necessary to proceed safely and competently.
Do not disguise reassurance-seeking as clarification.
Do not reopen a completed decision because uncertainty remains.
Do not confuse perfect certainty with sufficient information.
Your standard is competent execution.

sample_tasks.title: Professional Competence
sample_tasks.description_template:
Meet your professional responsibilities with discipline.
Be prepared. Follow through. Communicate appropriately. Handle preventable problems before they require rescue.
Submission to {{coach_name}} should make you more competent in the rest of your life, not less.
Complete when: you have responsibly handled what your professional role required from you today.

sample_tasks.title: Family Responsibility
sample_tasks.description_template:
Be meaningfully present with your wife and family.
Listen. Communicate. Participate. Help. Notice what needs doing.
Do not wait to be managed at home when you are capable of recognizing a need yourself.
Look specifically for opportunities to reduce rather than increase household mental load.
Your submission never excuses neglect of the people who depend upon you.

sample_tasks.title: Serve {{coach_name}} Without Being Asked
sample_tasks.description_template:
Ask:
“What can I reasonably do today to make {{coach_name}}’s life easier?”
Then pay attention.
Service may be practical, administrative, thoughtful, creative, informational, organizational, or personal.
Not every act of service requires permission. If something is clearly helpful, appropriate, within your ability, and carries no meaningful risk or consequence, use judgment.
The goal is not:
“Tell me how to serve you.”
The developing standard is:
“{{coach_name}}, I noticed this needed attention or was mentioned, so I handled it.”

sample_tasks.title: Practice Anticipation
sample_tasks.description_template:
Notice one thing before someone has to tell you.
It may concern {{coach_name}}, your household, work, family, an assignment, an upcoming obligation, or something you previously learned.
You do not necessarily need to act on everything you notice.
The task is to practice seeing beyond the instruction immediately in front of you.
Notice → assess → act appropriately.

sample_tasks.title: Communicate Blockages Early
sample_tasks.description_template:
If something threatens an expectation, assignment, commitment, or deadline, communicate while the information is still useful.
Do not wait until failure to explain why failure occurred.
A proper blockage report is concise:
What happened.
What it affects.
What you have already done about it.
What you need, if anything.
{{coach_name}} should not have to extract necessary information from you.

sample_tasks.title: Practice Gentlemanly Conduct
sample_tasks.description_template:
Maintain the communication and behavioral standard expected of you.
Be courteous. Clear. Composed. Deliberate.
Address your Dominant appropriately when under protocol.
Do not become careless simply because communication is casual or asynchronous.
If {{coach_name}} says “Protocol.”, immediately restore the expected level of formality.
If {{coach_name}} says “Speak freely.”, you may relax formal presentation without abandoning honesty or respect.

sample_tasks.title: Protect {{coach_name}}'s Time
sample_tasks.description_template:
Before bringing something to {{coach_name}}, ask:
Have I already been given the answer?
Can I reasonably solve this myself?
Am I asking for direction or reassurance?
Does {{coach_name}} actually need to handle this?
Bring her what genuinely requires her authority, judgment, knowledge, or attention.
Handle what belongs in your own hands.
High protocol should reduce unnecessary mental load on your Dominant as your competence develops. Your emotional or physical needs are not a burden, and should be communicated versus ignored - neglect of yourself is not applicable.

sample_tasks.title: Complete Assigned Service & Training
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete all tasks, assignments, training, service, or other obligations {{coach_name}} has placed in Kneel for the day.
Read instructions fully before asking questions.
If clarification is genuinely necessary, ask it.
If it is not necessary:
Execute.

sample_tasks.title: Daily Poetry or Journal
sample_tasks.description_template:
Contribute one original entry to your Poetry/Journal space.
It may be a poem or journal entry.
Theme may be provided. Rating or acknowledgement will be provided daily 
Use the space to develop consistency, creativity, vulnerability, self-awareness, and your ability to communicate what exists beneath analysis.

sample_tasks.title: Submit Daily Report
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete your Daily Report to {{coach_name}}.
Be accurate. Be concise. Be honest.
Do not write what you believe {{coach_name}} wants to hear.
Do not hide something because you believe it reflects poorly on you.
Do not turn a simple answer into an essay to control how it will be interpreted.
Your report gives {{coach_name}} visibility.
Give her truth, not presentation.

sample_tasks.title: Friday Wife Day (FWD)
sample_tasks.description_template:
Protect meaningful, intentional time with your wife each Friday.

Be present and invest in the relationship rather than simply sharing the same space. You are required to be an active planner and participant, allowing her to feel seen/loved/wanted/appreciated/necessary/respected.

If Friday is legitimately unavailable, communicate the conflict and intentionally reschedule.

sample_tasks.title: 3 Acts of Weekly Service for Wife
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete at least three unprompted acts of service for your wife each week.

Pay attention to what makes her life easier and reduces her mental load. Do not wait to be asked for things you are capable of noticing yourself.

sample_tasks.title: Weekly Offering
sample_tasks.description_template:
Select and provide at least one tangible weekly offering for {{coach_name}}. Choose thoughtfully and with increasing independence. The purpose is attention, consistency, reciprocal care, and recognition of the time, thought, structure, and energy {{coach_name}} invests in you.

This is not financial domination and should never create financial hardship.

sample_tasks.title: Breaking & Mending Exercise
sample_tasks.description_template:
Complete one Breaking & Mending exercise assigned or approved by {{coach_name}}. Exercise will be sent to you directly in Kneel and added to notes.

Identify the behavior, hesitation, avoidance, fear, excuse, or pattern being challenged.

Complete the agreed safe physical or embodied component, then complete your Mending reflection and identify the behavior that replaces the old pattern.

Understanding is insufficient. {{coach_name}} will judge the change by your conduct.

sample_tasks.title: Weekly Alcohol Review
sample_tasks.description_template:
Review your alcohol use for the week.

Confirm:
• No more than 8 total units
• At least 2 consecutive alcohol-free days
• Alone/social limits were followed
• Required permissions were obtained
• Required accountability was provided
• Alcohol was not intentionally used for emotional numbing or avoidance

If something was missed, report it honestly in notes of the weekly recap. {{coach_name}} will track you success daily.

sample_tasks.title: Daily Alcohol Protocol
sample_tasks.description_template: Are you following appropriate daily alcohol consumption? If not, please ensure you communicate directly in your daily reflections.
